title: Law Commission proposes sweeping product liability reforms to bring AI and software within scope
key_facts: The UK Law Commission launched a consultation on 8 Oct 2026 on reforming product liability law.
The proposals would widen the definition of 'product' to include software and AI systems, and bring online platforms within scope.
The reforms would introduce new rights of consumer redress if a product is deemed defective and clarify when people harmed are entitled to compensation.
The current law was introduced almost 40 years ago, before smartphones, apps, social media and AI, and was limited to physical items.
Professor Solène Rowan, Commissioner for Commercial and Common Law, said the law must evolve with technology.
The consultation closes on 14 January 2027; final recommendations are expected in late 2027.
quote_evidence: The UK Law Commission today (8 October) launched a consultation on major reform to bring product liability law up to date, including expanding the definition of "product" to include software and AI systems.
The consultation closes on Thursday 14 January 2027.
Following the consultation, the Law Commission will consider all responses before publishing its final recommendations for reform, expected in late 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: A proposal to make makers of AI and software liable under product defect law.
notes: Proposal and consultation only; not law. Legal IT Insider relays the Law Commission announcement.
